name: Banana
npk_ratio: Target ratio approx. 3 : 1 : 6 (N : P2O5 : K2O). Mineral blend: 365g Sulphate of Ammonia (21% N) : 270g Superphosphate (9.1% P2O5) : 365g Sulphate of Potash (41.5% K2O) per 1kg batch. Resulting analysis: ~7.67% N, 2.46% P2O5, 15.15% K2O.
dosing_rules: Start at 50g of blend per clump per application. Frequency: every 4-6 weeks while actively growing. Spread thinly across the wider root zone, not a tight ring. Apply to moist soil, water in gently afterwards. Reduce or pause over winter if growth visibly slows. Hold at 50g for at least a full season before increasing.
seasonal_notes: Spring-Summer: feed every 4-6 weeks, 50g. Autumn: taper to 30-50g. Winter: pause feeding unless still actively growing. Soil test before applying dolomite. Spring: resume full feeding 2-3 weeks clear of any winter dolomite.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing between veins, veins stay green: Magnesium deficiency. General pale yellowing, slow growth: Nitrogen deficiency. Dark green leaves, weak stems, poor bunch fill: Potassium deficiency. Brown scorched leaf margins, wilting: Over-fertilising. Purplish/reddish leaf tinge: Phosphorus deficiency.
mulch_notes: Depth: approx 10cm organic mulch. Keep clear of stems. Sequence: pull mulch back, apply fertiliser, water in, replace mulch. Top up every 2-3 months. Sucker thinning: keep main stem plus 1-2 followers, remove extras while small.

name: Tomato
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O) during fruiting; lower N once flowering starts. Phosphorus important early for root/flower development; then potassium for fruit fill. Calcium also important.
dosing_rules: Start at 15-20g balanced blend per plant every 2-3 weeks once flowering begins. Avoid heavy nitrogen once fruiting starts; it pushes leafy growth over fruit. Water consistently.
seasonal_notes: Spring: feed lightly as seedlings establish. Summer (flowering/fruiting): feed every 2-3 weeks; reduce N; maintain K and Ca. Autumn: taper off as plant finishes.
deficiency_guide: Blossom end rot (dark sunken patch on fruit base): calcium deficiency; often linked to inconsistent watering. Yellowing lower leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Purple-tinged leaves: phosphorus deficiency. Curling upper leaves: potassium deficiency or heat stress.
mulch_notes: Depth approx 7-10cm straw or sugarcane mulch; keep clear of stem base. Helps maintain even soil moisture which reduces blossom end rot risk.

name: Basil
npk_ratio: Light feeder. Avoid high nitrogen; produces lush but less aromatic leaves and dilutes essential oils. A mild balanced liquid feed is preferable to a strong granular blend.
dosing_rules: Small handful of balanced blend; or diluted liquid seaweed/fish emulsion; once monthly. Prioritise consistent light watering over heavy feeding. Pinch flower buds to extend leaf production.
seasonal_notes: Spring-Autumn: feed monthly while actively growing. Basil is frost tender and will die off in cold weather. In tropical/subtropical zones may persist year round with light feeding continuing.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing lower leaves: nitrogen deficiency; correct with a mild feed. Leggy pale growth: insufficient light rather than nutrients. Bitter flavour; rapid flowering: heat/moisture stress rather than a nutrient issue.
mulch_notes: Light mulch only; a thin layer of straw or compost; kept well clear of the stem. Basil prefers free-draining soil.

name: Citrus
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O). Citrus are moderate-heavy nitrogen feeders for leaf flush with good potassium for fruit development. Magnesium deficiency common.
dosing_rules: Apply a citrus-specific or balanced blend around the drip line (not against the trunk) every 6-8 weeks during active growth. Water in well. Reduce over winter.
seasonal_notes: Spring: main feed as flowering begins. Summer: continue regular feeding through fruit development. Autumn: light feed. Winter: pause or reduce; citrus growth slows in cooler months.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing between veins on older leaves (veins stay green): Magnesium deficiency, common in citrus. General pale yellowing new growth: Nitrogen deficiency. Poor fruit set or small fruit: Potassium or boron deficiency. Leaf curl with grey specks: pest (citrus leafminer) rather than nutrient issue.
mulch_notes: Depth approx 10cm organic mulch kept well clear of the trunk collar. Citrus are shallow rooted and benefit from consistent moisture retention. Avoid mounding mulch against trunk, encourages collar rot.

name: Capsicum
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O) during fruiting; similar profile to tomato as both are nightshades. Calcium important to prevent blossom end rot.
dosing_rules: Start at 15-20g balanced blend per plant every 3-4 weeks once flowering begins. Avoid excess nitrogen once fruiting starts. Water consistently to support calcium uptake.
seasonal_notes: Spring: feed lightly as seedlings establish. Summer (flowering/fruiting): feed every 3-4 weeks. Autumn: taper off. More heat tolerant than tomato, can continue later into warm season.
deficiency_guide: Blossom end rot (dark sunken patch on fruit): calcium deficiency, often linked to inconsistent watering. Yellowing lower leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Poor fruit set: potassium or heat stress.
mulch_notes: Depth approx 7-10cm straw or sugarcane mulch, keep clear of stem base. Helps maintain even soil moisture.

name: Chilli
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O); similar profile to capsicum and tomato as nightshades. Light feeder relative to tomato, excess nitrogen reduces fruit heat/flavour.
dosing_rules: Start at 10-15g balanced blend per plant every 4-5 weeks. Avoid heavy nitrogen, which encourages leaf growth over fruit and chilli heat development.
seasonal_notes: Spring: feed lightly as seedlings establish. Summer-Autumn: feed every 4-5 weeks through extended fruiting season, chillies often fruit longer than tomato/capsicum in SEQ.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing lower leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Dropped flowers: heat stress or inconsistent watering rather than nutrient issue. Poor fruit set: potassium deficiency.
mulch_notes: Depth approx 7-10cm straw mulch, keep clear of stem base.

name: Silverbeet
npk_ratio: Light-moderate nitrogen feeder. Leafy green, harvested continuously (cut-and-come-again) rather than once, so little and often feeding suits better than heavy single doses.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend or diluted liquid feed every 3-4 weeks. Keep soil consistently moist, inconsistent watering causes bitter or tough leaves.
seasonal_notes: Best grown autumn through early spring in SEQ, bolts (goes to seed) and becomes bitter in full summer heat. Harvest outer leaves continuously, allowing centre to keep producing.
deficiency_guide: Pale yellowing leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Bitter or tough leaves: inconsistent watering or heat stress. Bolting (flowering early): heat stress or overcrowding.
mulch_notes: Light mulch layer approx 5cm, straw or compost, keep clear of crown of the plant.

name: Lettuce
npk_ratio: Light nitrogen feeder. Fast growing leafy green, excess nitrogen can cause soft growth prone to pests and disease.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend or diluted liquid feed every 2-3 weeks given fast growth cycle. Keep soil consistently moist.
seasonal_notes: Best grown autumn through early spring in SEQ, bolts and turns bitter quickly in summer heat. Succession plant every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest.
deficiency_guide: Pale yellowing leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Bitter taste, bolting: heat stress. Tip burn on leaves: calcium deficiency or irregular watering.
mulch_notes: Light mulch layer approx 5cm, keep clear of stem base to avoid rot in humid conditions.

name: Carrot
npk_ratio: Ratio favours potassium over nitrogen, approx 1:1:2 (N:P2O5:K2O). Excess nitrogen causes excess leafy top growth and can cause forked roots.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed at planting, avoid fresh manure right before sowing. Side dress lightly with potassium-focused feed once roots begin to swell, around 6 weeks in.
seasonal_notes: Best grown autumn through winter into early spring in SEQ, cooler soil temperatures suit root development better than summer heat.
deficiency_guide: Forked or hairy roots: excess nitrogen or fresh manure, or rocky/compacted soil. Pale foliage: nitrogen deficiency, though usually not yield-limiting for the root itself. Small roots: potassium deficiency or overcrowding, thin seedlings properly.
mulch_notes: Light mulch only, keep away from direct contact with the root crown, helps retain even moisture which produces straighter roots.

name: Beetroot
npk_ratio: Ratio favours potassium over nitrogen, approx 1:1:2 (N:P2O5:K2O), similar to carrot. Avoid excess nitrogen, which favours leaf growth over root bulb development.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed at planting, side dress lightly with potassium-focused feed once bulbs begin to swell, around 5-6 weeks in.
seasonal_notes: Best grown autumn through winter into early spring in SEQ, similar window to carrot.
deficiency_guide: Small or woody bulbs: potassium deficiency or overcrowding. Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency, generally not critical to the root itself. Cracked bulbs: irregular watering.
mulch_notes: Light mulch only, keep clear of the crown where leaves emerge from the bulb.

name: Strawberry
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, balanced ratio approx 2:1:2 (N:P2O5:K2O). Prefers slightly acidic soil. Fruits over an extended period, benefits from smaller frequent feeds rather than one heavy dose.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend every 3-4 weeks through flowering and fruiting. Avoid high nitrogen once fruiting begins, favours leaf growth over fruit.
seasonal_notes: Plant autumn in SEQ for a winter-spring fruiting season, cooler climate crop that struggles in full summer heat and humidity. Manage runners to avoid overcrowding.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Poor fruit set or small fruit: potassium deficiency. Fruit rot in humid weather: overcrowding/poor airflow rather than a nutrient issue, thin runners and mulch to keep fruit off damp soil.
mulch_notes: Depth approx 5-7cm straw mulch specifically, keeps fruit clean and off damp soil reducing rot risk, classic strawberry mulch choice for good reason.

name: Nectarine
npk_ratio: Moderate nitrogen with good potassium during fruit swell, approx ratio 2:1:2 (N:P2O5:K2O). Deciduous fruit tree.
dosing_rules: Apply balanced blend around the drip line in early spring as buds swell, and again after harvest to support next season's growth. Avoid feeding late autumn/winter while dormant.
seasonal_notes: Plant while dormant in winter. Spring: feed as buds swell. Summer: fruit development and harvest. After harvest: light feed to support recovery growth. Variety matters significantly in SEQ; low-chill varieties bred for subtropical climates perform far better than standard southern varieties due to mild winters.
deficiency_guide: Leaf curl (puckered, reddish, distorted leaves in spring): fungal disease (not nutrient related), prune for airflow and consider preventative copper spray at leaf drop. Poor fruit set: inadequate winter chill for the variety, or potassium deficiency. Small fruit: overcrowding, thin fruit while small.
mulch_notes: Depth approx 10cm organic mulch kept clear of trunk base. Prune annually for airflow and shape, thin fruit to improve size and reduce limb stress.

name: Eggplant
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O), nightshade family, potassium important for fruit development.
dosing_rules: 15-20g balanced blend per plant every 4 weeks once flowering begins.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Dec, harvest 10-14 weeks later Dec-Apr. Long cropping season in SEQ warmth.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing lower leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Dropped flowers: heat/water stress. Bitter fruit: water stress or over-mature picking.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm straw mulch, keep clear of stem base.

name: Cucumber
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O), vigorous vine, heavy water and potassium needs during fruiting.
dosing_rules: 20g balanced blend every 3 weeks once vines are running and flowering.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Feb, harvest 8-10 weeks later Oct-Apr. Avoid waterlogging in humid wet season.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Bitter fruit: water stress. Powdery mildew on leaves: fungal, not nutrient related, improve airflow.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm straw mulch, trellis to improve airflow and reduce fungal issues.

name: Zucchini
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O), vigorous grower, moderate-heavy feeder.
dosing_rules: 20g balanced blend every 3 weeks once flowering and fruiting begins.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Jan, harvest 8 weeks later Oct-Mar. Pick young and often to keep plant productive.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Poor fruit set: lack of pollination or potassium deficiency. Powdery mildew: fungal, improve airflow.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm straw mulch, keep clear of stem base to reduce crown rot risk.

name: Pumpkin
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 2:1:3 (N:P2O5:K2O), long season crop, benefits from steady light feeding over heavy single doses.
dosing_rules: 20-30g balanced blend every 5 weeks, increase slightly once fruit is setting.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Dec, long season, harvest 14-20 weeks later Feb-May.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Poor fruit set: pollination issue or potassium deficiency. Fruit rot on ground contact: raise fruit off damp soil.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm straw mulch, vines sprawl widely, mulch whole bed area not just base.

name: Choko
npk_ratio: Light feeder, vigorous self-sufficient vine once established, ratio approx 1:1:2.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed every 6 weeks during active growth, established vines need minimal feeding.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct from a sprouted fruit, harvest autumn-winter Mar-Jun. Very low maintenance once established on a trellis.
deficiency_guide: Poor fruiting: insufficient trellis space or shade. Generally trouble-free once established.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch at base, needs sturdy trellis or fence to climb.

name: Snake Beans
npk_ratio: Legume, fixes own nitrogen, low N requirement, ratio approx 1:1:2.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed at planting only, avoid high nitrogen fertiliser which legumes don't need.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Feb, harvest 8-10 weeks later Nov-Apr. Heat tolerant, good SEQ summer crop.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves uncommon given nitrogen fixing. Poor pod set: potassium deficiency or inadequate pollination.
mulch_notes: Depth 7cm mulch, provide trellis for climbing varieties.

name: Climbing Beans
npk_ratio: Legume, fixes own nitrogen, low N requirement, ratio approx 1:1:2.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed at planting only, avoid excess nitrogen.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Mar, harvest 8-10 weeks later Oct-May.
deficiency_guide: Poor pod set: potassium deficiency or pollination issue. Pale leaves uncommon.
mulch_notes: Depth 7cm mulch, needs trellis or stakes.

name: Dwarf Beans
npk_ratio: Legume, fixes own nitrogen, low N requirement, ratio approx 1:1:2.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed at planting only.
seasonal_notes: Two windows in SEQ: plant Feb-Apr and Aug-Oct, harvest 8-9 weeks later.
deficiency_guide: Poor pod set: potassium deficiency. Pale leaves uncommon.
mulch_notes: Depth 5-7cm mulch, no trellis needed given bush habit.

name: Sweet Corn
npk_ratio: Heavy nitrogen feeder relative to other vegetables, ratio approx 3:1:2.
dosing_rules: 25-30g balanced blend every 3 weeks, side dress with extra nitrogen when stalks are knee-high.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Jan, harvest 12-14 weeks later Nov-Apr. Plant in blocks not single rows for pollination.
deficiency_guide: Pale striped leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Poorly filled cobs: inadequate pollination from planting in rows rather than blocks, or potassium deficiency.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch, shallow roots benefit from consistent moisture.

name: Okra
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, heat loving and well suited to SEQ summer.
dosing_rules: 15-20g balanced blend every 4 weeks once flowering begins.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Jan, harvest 8 weeks later Dec-Apr. Harvest pods young and often, tough if left too long.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Poor pod set: potassium deficiency or heat stress.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch, keep clear of stem base.

name: Asian Greens
npk_ratio: Light feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, fast growing leafy brassica group (bok choy, pak choy, choy sum).
dosing_rules: Small handful or diluted liquid feed every 2-3 weeks given fast growth cycle.
seasonal_notes: Plant Feb-Nov in SEQ (avoid hottest peak summer), harvest 5-6 weeks later, succession plant for continuous supply.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Bolting (early flowering): heat stress, plant in cooler months for best results.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm, keep clear of stem base.

name: Spinach
npk_ratio: Light feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, true (English) spinach, cool season crop.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend every 3-4 weeks.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Aug, harvest 6-8 weeks later. Struggles and bolts in SEQ summer heat and humidity.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Bolting/bitter leaves: heat stress, stick to cooler months.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm, keep soil consistently moist.

name: Rocket
npk_ratio: Very light feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, fast growing and peppery, flavour intensifies in heat/stress.
dosing_rules: Minimal feeding needed, light balanced feed every 4 weeks if growth is slow.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Sep, harvest 4-6 weeks later, continuous cut-and-come-again.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Excessively hot/bitter flavour: heat stress, more pronounced in warmer months.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm.

name: Cabbage
npk_ratio: Moderate-heavy feeder relative to other brassicas, ratio approx 3:1:2.
dosing_rules: 20-25g balanced blend every 3-4 weeks through head development.
seasonal_notes: Plant Feb-Jun, harvest 10-12 weeks later May-Sep.
deficiency_guide: Pale outer leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Loose, small heads: insufficient feeding or spacing. Split heads: irregular watering.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch, keep clear of stem base.

name: Broccoli
npk_ratio: Moderate-heavy feeder, ratio approx 3:1:2.
dosing_rules: 20g balanced blend every 3-4 weeks through head development.
seasonal_notes: Plant Feb-May, harvest 12-14 weeks later May-Aug.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Small or premature flowering heads: heat stress or inconsistent feeding.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch, keep clear of stem base.

name: Cauliflower
npk_ratio: Heavy feeder relative to other brassicas, fussy about consistency, ratio approx 3:1:2.
dosing_rules: 20-25g balanced blend every 3 weeks, needs very consistent feeding and watering for good heads.
seasonal_notes: Plant Feb-Apr, harvest 14-16 weeks later Jun-Sep.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Small, loose, or discoloured curds: inconsistent feeding/watering, or insufficient boron.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch, very sensitive to any growth check, keep consistently moist.

name: Kale
npk_ratio: Light-moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, hardy and relatively trouble-free.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend every 4 weeks.
seasonal_notes: Plant Feb-Jul, harvest continuously from 8 weeks through to Oct. More heat tolerant than most brassicas.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Tough leaves: under-watering or over-mature leaves, harvest younger leaves regularly.
mulch_notes: Depth 7cm mulch, keep clear of stem base.

name: Radish
npk_ratio: Very light feeder, ratio favours potassium approx 1:1:2, fastest growing root vegetable.
dosing_rules: Minimal feeding needed, light balanced feed at planting only, excess feeding reduces root quality.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Sep, harvest 4-6 weeks later, very quick turnaround, good for succession planting.
deficiency_guide: Forked/split roots: excess nitrogen or compacted soil. Pithy/hollow roots: left in ground too long or heat stress.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm, keep soil loose and well-drained.

name: Sweet Potato
npk_ratio: Low nitrogen requirement, ratio favours potassium approx 1:1:3, excess nitrogen produces vine growth at the expense of tubers.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed at planting, avoid further nitrogen feeding, side dress lightly with potassium mid-season if needed.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Dec, long season, harvest 4-5 months later Feb-May. Vigorous vine, well suited to SEQ warmth.
deficiency_guide: Excess vine with few tubers: too much nitrogen. Small tubers: potassium deficiency or overcrowding.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch at planting, vines will self-mulch as they spread.

name: Potato
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:3, avoid fresh manure which can cause scab and poor tuber shape.
dosing_rules: 20g balanced blend at planting and again when shoots are 15-20cm tall (hilling stage).
seasonal_notes: Two windows in SEQ: plant Feb-Apr and Aug-Sep, harvest 90-120 days later.
deficiency_guide: Small or green tubers: insufficient hilling (soil mounding) exposing tubers to light. Scabby skin: excess fresh manure or alkaline soil.
mulch_notes: Depth 10-15cm mulch/soil hilled progressively as shoots grow, this is essential for tuber development, not optional.

name: Onion
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, long season crop.
dosing_rules: 15-20g balanced blend every 4-5 weeks through bulb development, reduce nitrogen as bulbs begin to swell.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-May, long season, harvest 5-6 months later Sep-Nov.
deficiency_guide: Thin necks/poor bulbing: excess nitrogen late in season. Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency early on.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm, keep clear of the bulb itself to avoid rot.

name: Garlic
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2.
dosing_rules: 15-20g balanced blend every 5 weeks, reduce nitrogen in final 4-6 weeks before harvest to help bulbs cure.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-May, long season, harvest 5-6 months later Sep-Oct. Benefits from a cooler establishment period.
deficiency_guide: Small bulbs/few cloves: insufficient feeding early, or excess nitrogen late preventing proper bulb maturity.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm, keep clear of the bulb.

name: Ginger
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, rhizome crop, prefers dappled shade and consistent moisture.
dosing_rules: 20g balanced blend every 6 weeks through the growing season.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct, long season, harvest 8-10 months later Jun-Sep.
deficiency_guide: Pale/yellowing leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Small rhizomes: insufficient feeding or inadequate moisture through the season.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch, helps retain the consistent moisture ginger needs, grow in part shade in SEQ heat.

name: Turmeric
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, similar growing requirements to ginger.
dosing_rules: 20g balanced blend every 6 weeks through the growing season.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Oct, long season, harvest 9-10 months later Jul-Sep.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Small rhizomes: insufficient feeding or moisture stress.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch, grow in part shade with consistent moisture.

name: Parsley
npk_ratio: Light feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, biennial often grown as an annual herb.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend every 5 weeks, or diluted liquid feed more often.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Sep (cooler months best), harvest continuously from 10 weeks.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Slow growth: insufficient light or heat stress in summer.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm.

name: Coriander
npk_ratio: Light feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, short lived and prone to bolting in heat.
dosing_rules: Minimal feeding needed, light balanced feed at planting only.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Aug (cooler months, bolts quickly in heat), harvest continuously 6-8 weeks before it bolts to seed.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Rapid bolting to flower/seed: heat stress, this is the main challenge growing coriander in SEQ.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm, keep consistently moist.

name: Mint
npk_ratio: Very light feeder, ratio approx 1:1:1, vigorous and can become invasive, best grown in a pot.
dosing_rules: Minimal feeding needed, light balanced feed every 6-8 weeks.
seasonal_notes: Plant any time, grows year-round in SEQ with consistent moisture. Confine to a pot to prevent spreading.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency, uncommon given vigour. Leggy growth: insufficient light.
mulch_notes: Light mulch if in-ground, not needed if potted.

name: Chives
npk_ratio: Light feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, allium family herb.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend every 5-6 weeks.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Sep, harvest continuously from 8 weeks, cut outer leaves and allow regrowth.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Slow regrowth after cutting: insufficient feeding or overharvesting too frequently.
mulch_notes: Light mulch 5cm.

name: Thyme
npk_ratio: Very light feeder, ratio approx 1:1:1, drought tolerant Mediterranean herb, dislikes excess moisture and rich soil.
dosing_rules: Minimal feeding needed, light balanced feed every 8 weeks, avoid overfeeding which reduces aromatic oil concentration.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Oct, perennial, harvest continuously year-round once established.
deficiency_guide: Leggy, weak growth: overwatering or overfeeding, thyme prefers lean conditions. Woody unproductive growth: needs periodic hard pruning.
mulch_notes: Avoid thick mulch, thyme prefers free-draining, drier conditions at the base.

name: Oregano
npk_ratio: Very light feeder, ratio approx 1:1:1, similar preferences to thyme, drought tolerant.
dosing_rules: Minimal feeding needed, light balanced feed every 8 weeks.
seasonal_notes: Plant Mar-Oct, perennial, harvest continuously year-round once established.
deficiency_guide: Leggy growth: overwatering/overfeeding. Reduced flavour: excess feeding or insufficient sun.
mulch_notes: Light mulch only, avoid excess moisture retention at the base.

name: Rosemary
npk_ratio: Very light feeder, ratio approx 1:1:1, drought tolerant perennial shrub.
dosing_rules: Minimal feeding needed, light balanced feed every 10 weeks, established plants need very little.
seasonal_notes: Plant any time avoiding peak summer heat, perennial shrub, harvest continuously year-round once established.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing leaves: usually overwatering or poor drainage rather than nutrient deficiency. Leggy growth: needs pruning after flowering.
mulch_notes: Avoid thick mulch, rosemary prefers free-draining, drier soil.

name: Vietnamese Mint
npk_ratio: Light feeder, ratio approx 1:1:1, likes moisture and warmth, grows well in SEQ.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend every 6 weeks.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Mar (warm months), harvest continuously once established.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Slow growth: insufficient warmth or moisture.
mulch_notes: Light mulch, keep consistently moist.

name: Lemongrass
npk_ratio: Light-moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:1, clumping perennial grass.
dosing_rules: Small handful balanced blend every 6-8 weeks during warm growing season.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Feb, perennial clump, harvest continuously once established by cutting outer stems.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Slow growth: cold stress, growth slows noticeably over winter.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm mulch around the base of the clump.

name: Mango
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:3, excess nitrogen reduces flowering and fruit set.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around the drip line every 8 weeks during active growth, avoid heavy nitrogen close to flowering time.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Sep, established tree flowers in winter-spring, harvest Nov-Feb depending on variety.
deficiency_guide: Poor flowering/fruit set: excess nitrogen or insufficient dry period before flowering. Small fruit: potassium deficiency.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk, mature trees are relatively drought tolerant.

name: Avocado
npk_ratio: Moderate-heavy feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, sensitive to root rot from overwatering/poor drainage.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around the drip line every 8 weeks, water deeply but ensure good drainage.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct, harvest timing varies widely by variety, generally Apr-Dec.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing leaves with brown tips: salt sensitivity or overwatering. Poor fruit set: inadequate pollination or young tree age (can take years to fruit).
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk, critical to avoid overwatering, avocados are very sensitive to waterlogged roots.

name: Pawpaw
npk_ratio: Heavy feeder given fast growth rate, ratio approx 3:1:3.
dosing_rules: 20-30g balanced blend every 4 weeks, fast growing and short lived (3-5 years), needs steady feeding.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Nov, fast growing, fruits within a year, then continuously year-round once mature.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency, fast growth rate makes this show quickly. Poor fruit set: needs a male plant nearby for pollination unless self-fertile variety.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk base, shallow roots benefit from consistent moisture.

name: Macadamia
npk_ratio: Slow growing, moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around drip line every 12 weeks, slow growing tree needs patience, takes years to bear well.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct, very slow to mature (5-10 years to good production), nuts drop progressively Mar-Sep.
deficiency_guide: Poor nut fill: insufficient feeding over the long establishment period, or lack of a second variety nearby for cross-pollination.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk.

name: Fig
npk_ratio: Low-moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, drought tolerant once established.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around drip line every 8 weeks during growing season, reduce once established as figs tolerate neglect well.
seasonal_notes: Plant Jun-Aug while dormant, harvest Dec-Mar, often two crops per year in warm climates.
deficiency_guide: Fruit drop before ripening: inconsistent watering. Poor fruiting: excess nitrogen favouring leaf growth over fruit.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk.

name: Mulberry
npk_ratio: Vigorous grower, low feeding requirement, ratio approx 2:1:2.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around drip line every 8 weeks during active growth.
seasonal_notes: Plant Jun-Aug while dormant, harvest Sep-Nov, vigorous and generally trouble-free.
deficiency_guide: Few issues typically, very hardy. Poor fruiting: usually just young tree age.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk.

name: Lychee
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:3, potassium important for fruit development, sensitive to frost when young.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around drip line every 8 weeks, reduce nitrogen as flowering approaches to encourage fruit set over leaf growth.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct, protect young trees from any frost, harvest Nov-Jan.
deficiency_guide: Poor flowering: excess nitrogen or insufficient cool period before flowering. Fruit drop: inconsistent watering during fruit development.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk, protect young trees from cold snaps.

name: Guava
npk_ratio: Hardy, moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, often fruits more than once a year.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around drip line every 8 weeks during growing season.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct, harvest Feb-May and often again later in the year, very productive and low-maintenance.
deficiency_guide: Few issues typically, very hardy and tolerant of poor soil. Fruit fly can affect ripening fruit, not a nutrient issue.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk.

name: Dragon Fruit
npk_ratio: Low feeder, ratio favours potassium approx 1:1:2, climbing cactus, needs sturdy trellis support.
dosing_rules: Light balanced feed every 6 weeks during growing season, avoid overfeeding which this cactus doesn't need.
seasonal_notes: Plant Sep-Nov, harvest Dec-Apr, needs a sturdy trellis or post, flowers at night and may need hand pollination for best fruit set.
deficiency_guide: Poor fruit set: inadequate pollination, hand pollinate at night if fruit set is low. Stem rot: overwatering or poor drainage.
mulch_notes: Avoid heavy mulch directly against the stem base, this cactus prefers drier conditions at the base.

name: Custard Apple
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around drip line every 8 weeks during growing season.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct, harvest Mar-Jun.
deficiency_guide: Poor fruit set: inadequate pollination, hand pollination often improves yield significantly for this fruit. Fruit drop: inconsistent watering.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of trunk.

name: Passionfruit
npk_ratio: Vigorous vine, heavy feeder, ratio approx 2:1:3, potassium important for fruit development.
dosing_rules: 20-25g balanced blend every 4 weeks during growing season, vigorous vine needs sturdy trellis and steady feeding.
seasonal_notes: Plant Aug-Oct, harvest Feb-Jun, relatively short-lived vine (5-7 years), replace periodically for best production.
deficiency_guide: Pale leaves: nitrogen deficiency. Poor fruit set: inadequate pollination or potassium deficiency. Fruit drop: water stress.
mulch_notes: Depth 10cm mulch kept clear of the base, needs a sturdy trellis or fence.

name: Blueberry
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, requires acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5), use sulfate-based fertilisers and avoid lime/dolomite.
dosing_rules: Balanced acidic-specialty blend every 6 weeks during growing season, avoid any lime or dolomite application near this plant.
seasonal_notes: Plant Apr-Jun (cooler months), harvest Aug-Nov.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing between veins: iron deficiency, usually caused by soil pH being too high (not acidic enough) rather than lack of iron itself. Poor fruit set: insufficient pollination or soil pH too high.
mulch_notes: Depth 7-10cm acidic mulch such as pine bark or similar, helps maintain the acidic soil blueberries need.

name: Raspberry
npk_ratio: Moderate feeder, ratio approx 2:1:2, less reliable in SEQ heat and humidity than cooler climates, prefers afternoon shade here.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend every 6 weeks during growing season.
seasonal_notes: Plant Apr-Jun, harvest Sep-Nov, provide afternoon shade and good airflow to manage SEQ humidity.
deficiency_guide: Poor fruiting: heat/humidity stress, more challenging crop in SEQ than cooler regions. Fruit rot: humidity and poor airflow, prune for better ventilation.
mulch_notes: Depth 7cm mulch, benefits from afternoon shade position in SEQ heat.

name: Coffee
npk_ratio: Ratio approx 3:1:2 (N:P2O5:K2O), moderate-heavy nitrogen feeder for continuous leafy growth, potassium important during cherry development. Magnesium deficiency common, similar to banana and citrus.
dosing_rules: Balanced blend around the drip line every 6-8 weeks during active growth (spring-autumn). Reduce over winter. Water in well, avoid fertilising in very dry conditions.
seasonal_notes: SEQ sits at the southern edge of coffee's comfortable range. Plant Sep-Nov in a sheltered, part-shaded spot (north/east wall or under taller canopy), protect from frost when young. Slow to mature, typically 3-4 years before first fruiting. Cherries ripen gradually over an extended period rather than all at once, harvest by picking ripe (red) cherries progressively.
deficiency_guide: Yellowing between veins on older leaves (veins stay green): Magnesium deficiency, common in coffee as in banana/citrus. General pale yellowing, slow growth: Nitrogen deficiency. Poor cherry fill or few flowers: Potassium deficiency or insufficient light. Leaf scorch: too much direct sun, coffee prefers filtered light or part shade in SEQ heat.
mulch_notes: Depth approx 10cm organic mulch kept clear of the trunk base. Consistent moisture is important, coffee doesn't tolerate prolonged dry spells well. Shelter from frost and harsh afternoon sun is more important for this plant than most other fruiting trees in the catalog.
